what: Stellantis makes cars under fourteen brands: Jeep, Ram, Chrysler, Dodge, Peugeot, Citroen, Fiat, Opel, Vauxhall, Alfa Romeo, Maserati and others, formed from the merger of Fiat Chrysler and PSA.
customers: Car buyers in North America and Europe, through dealer networks.
money: Peugeot, Citroen, Opel, Fiat and Vauxhall
moat: Jeep and Ram are two of the most profitable vehicle franchises in America, and the European brands give scale in a market where scale decides whether a carmaker survives.
risks: A $16.9B net loss and $12.7B of negative free cash flow: this is a company in serious trouble
American inventories were allowed to build and had to be discounted, destroying the margin
$54.0B of debt, though against $35.4B of cash
opportunities: 0.058 times sales on $176.9B of revenue: the market is pricing in a great deal of difficulty
Analysts see about 81% upside, with 8 covering the stock
New management has been cutting inventory and restoring dealer margins, and Jeep and Ram remain strong franchises
watch: North American shipments and dealer inventory levels, and whether free cash flow turns positive.
